meaning: certainly, surely, if I'm not mistaken...
mnemonic: 石 a stone, solid enough to lean on, except this one wobbles a bit. The meeting is at three. Ta, she can check it if you want it in writing: たしか.
notes: 確かに means definitely. 確か in front of a statement does the opposite, hedging it: fairly sure, would not swear to it.
sentence: 明日の会議は確か３時からだと思います。
sentence_meaning: If I'm not mistaken, the meeting tomorrow starts at 3:00.

mnemonic: 十 ten and 分 the parts, so all ten tenths of it. Money still in the account at month end, and enough left to chew a bun on the way home: じゅうぶん.
notes: Also written 充分. Careful: 十分 also reads じっぷん, meaning ten minutes, with the same two characters.
sentence: お金はまだ十分あります。
sentence_meaning: We still have plenty of money.

mnemonic: 米 rice measured out on the left, and 理 the sense a thing makes on the right. Ingredients weighed, then put in an order that works. That is the whole of it: りょうり.
notes: 料理する is to cook. 日本料理 is Japanese cuisine and 料理人 りょうりにん is a cook.
sentence: これは日本の料理です。
sentence_meaning: This is Japanese cooking.

mnemonic: Not the date, and nobody is asking for the date. The stretch of years when you were small enough to be in that park every single day: ころ.
notes: 子供の頃 is when I was a child. After a word it softens to ごろ: 三時頃 さんじごろ, around three.
sentence: 子供の頃、よくその公園で遊んだ。
sentence_meaning: I often played in that park when I was a kid.

mnemonic: You expected the painting to be alright. It is not alright, it is good, and you have said so twice before you have decided to: なかなか.
notes: With a positive it is better than expected. With a negative it is not easily: なかなか来ない, he is taking forever.
sentence: 彼女は絵がなかなか上手です。
sentence_meaning: She's pretty good at painting.

mnemonic: 正 pulling up exactly on the mark and 直 an eye looking dead ahead. Neither of them goes round anything. She gives you the answer you were hoping to avoid: しょうじき.
notes: 正直に言うと is to be honest. It works as a character trait and as the adverb.
sentence: 彼女はとても正直だ。
sentence_meaning: She's very honest.

mnemonic: Not your name, not your things. The one item you cannot put down, leave in the hotel safe, or ask somebody to mind: み.
notes: 身 is you as a physical person. 体 からだ is the body as an object. 自ら みずから is oneself as the one doing the acting. 身分 みぶん is your standing.
sentence: 旅行中は身の安全が第一です。
sentence_meaning: Personal safety is paramount while traveling.

mnemonic: Two helpings in and somebody comes round with a third. Your hand goes flat over the plate before you have thought about it. Not one more pie: いっぱい.
notes: お腹がいっぱい is full up. In front of a noun it means a lot of: 人がいっぱい.
sentence: お腹がいっぱいです。
sentence_meaning: I am full.

mnemonic: 羊 a sheep drawn 大 big, which was somebody's old idea of a fine thing. You stop dead in front of the picture and hold up everyone behind you: うつくしい.
notes: More written and more formal than きれい. きれい also covers clean and tidy; this one does not.
sentence: この絵は美しいです。
sentence_meaning: This picture is beautiful.

mnemonic: One forkful and the table goes quiet, because it is not sweet, it is far too sweet, and nobody wants to be the one to say so. Ah, my: あまい.
notes: Also indulgent and soft on people: 甘い親 is a lenient parent, and 甘える あまえる is trading on it.
sentence: このケーキは甘いですね。
sentence_meaning: This cake is sweet, isn't it?

mnemonic: Call him an architect and you get corrected before the sentence has landed. Not an architect. An artist. He is the one who put mushrooms in the risotto: むしろ.
notes: Corrects a comparison: not A, or rather B. Usually with より or というより in front of it.
sentence: 彼は建築家というよりむしろ芸術家ね。
sentence_meaning: He's an artist rather than an architect.

mnemonic: On a giraffe there is an absurd amount of it. You follow it up, and up, and run out of sky before you get to the head: くび.
notes: 首になる くびになる is to be fired, the same idea as getting the chop.
sentence: きりんの首は長い。
sentence_meaning: The neck of giraffes are long.

mnemonic: 咸 all of it landing on 心 a heart, and 情 a second heart tucked under 青. Two hearts in one word, which is about right for the subject. Can Joe explain any of it? かんじょう.
notes: The emotion itself. 感じ かんじ is the impression you get; 気持ち きもち is nearer a physical sensation.
sentence: 感情とは複雑なものです。
sentence_meaning: Emotions are complex things.

mnemonic: 周 a border drawn the whole way round. Cherry trees on every side of the house, so whichever window you open the view is the same one: まわり.
notes: The everyday word. 周囲 しゅうい is the same idea in writing.
sentence: 家の周りに桜の木があります。
sentence_meaning: There are cherry blossoms around the house.

mnemonic: 方 which way a thing faces, and 法 water finding the one route down. Not what to do. The road by which it gets done, and you would like it written out: ほうほう.
notes: 方法 is the method. やり方 やりかた is the more spoken way of doing it.
sentence: 日本語が上手になる方法を教えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please teach me a way to get good at Japanese.

mnemonic: もう pointed forwards again, with 一度 the single turn of the wheel. He said it once, nobody moved, so here it comes with exactly the same patience: もういちど.
notes: Built from もう and 一度 いちど, both already in the deck. もう一回 もういっかい does the same job.
sentence: もう一度言います。
sentence_meaning: I will say it one more time.

mnemonic: 辶 a road with something on it that is in no rush at all. The car in front has done forty for six miles and there is nowhere to pass: oh, so slow. おそい.
notes: Does slow and late both, so it is the opposite of 早い はやい and of 速い はやい at once.
sentence: 前の車はとても遅い。
sentence_meaning: The car in front is very slow.

mnemonic: 会 people gathering in under a roof, and 話 a tongue doing the work. Not one person talking. The part where it goes back and forth, which is the part that counts: かいわ.
notes: Same 話 as 話す はなす. 会話 is the exchange itself rather than the talking.
sentence: 親子の会話は大切です。
sentence_meaning: Conversation between parents and children is important.

mnemonic: 𠆢 a lid coming down onto 口 a mouth, the two halves meeting exactly. New shoes on, and you walk the length of the shop without thinking about your feet once: あう.
notes: Same reading as 会う あう, to meet. This one is things matching: shoes fitting, sums agreeing, 話が合う getting on with somebody.
sentence: この靴は私の足に合っている。
sentence_meaning: These shoes fit me.

meaning: to come around, to come along
mnemonic: やる doing and 来る coming, bolted together. Not simply arriving. Making the entire journey and turning up on the doorstep, big top and all, from France: やってくる.
notes: More vivid than 来る on its own. It carries the sense of having come all that way to get here.
sentence: フランスからサーカスがやって来ます。
sentence_meaning: A circus is coming from France.

mnemonic: Three 木 trees, and then a great many more. Twenty minutes in, the light has changed and you cannot hear the road any more: もり.
notes: 森 is the forest and 林 はやし is the wood. 森林 しんりん puts them together for woodland in general.
sentence: 私は森を歩くのが好きです。
sentence_meaning: I like to walk in the forest.

meaning: to move, to make a move
mnemonic: 重 something heavy with 力 power behind it, the same as 動く, except this time it is you doing the shoving. Six of you round one table: oo, go on, cuss if it helps. うごかす.
notes: 動く うごく is it moving. 動かす is you moving it.
sentence: みんなで大きいテーブルを動かします。
sentence_meaning: Everyone moves the big table together.

mnemonic: 能 whatever a thing turns out to be able to do, with 力 an arm bent hard at the elbow next to it. Not what he was hired for. What he can actually do: のうりょく.
notes: 能力がある is capable. 力 ちから on its own is strength; 能力 is capability.
sentence: 彼は能力のある社員です。
sentence_meaning: He's a capable employee.

mnemonic: 雨 up top, and whatever sits under it will not keep still. He came in from the yard blue round the mouth and could not get the cup to his face: flu, or just cold. ふるえる.
notes: 地震 じしん is an earthquake, the same 震. 震える is a person shaking rather than the ground.
sentence: 彼は寒くて震えていました。
sentence_meaning: He was cold and shivering.

mnemonic: 月 counting off the months, and 待 somebody stood outside the temple waiting. Everyone has decided in advance how this goes. Key in one hand, tie straightened: きたい.
notes: 期待する is to expect in the hopeful sense. 予想 よそう is a flat prediction with no hope in it.
sentence: みんな私たちに期待しています。
sentence_meaning: Everyone has expectations of us.

mnemonic: 無 everything burnt away to nothing and 事 a matter to deal with. No matters at all, which is the point. Home, and the budgie is still alive: ぶじ.
notes: 無事に is safely. It means nothing went wrong, not that nothing happened.
sentence: 無事、家に着きました。
sentence_meaning: I arrived home safely.

mnemonic: 走 running with 己 yourself behind it, the same standing-up as 起きる, except somebody made it happen. He threw the first punch and the whole street had a night of it: おこす.
notes: Same word as 起こす "to wake up". 起きる おきる is a thing happening by itself; 起こす is somebody causing it.
sentence: 彼は暴力事件を起こしたんだよ。
sentence_meaning: He caused a violent incident.

mnemonic: The very same 起こす. What you are standing upright this time is a person, at six in the morning, against their considerable preference: おこす.
notes: Same word as 起こす "to cause". 起きる おきる is getting up yourself; 起こす is getting somebody else up.
sentence: 明日、6時に起こしてください。
sentence_meaning: Please wake me up tomorrow at six o'clock.

mnemonic: A pictograph drawn side on, and you have two of them. Say something across the room and she turns the good one towards you: me? me? みみ.
notes: 耳がいい is good hearing. 聞く きく is the listening you do with it.
sentence: 彼女は耳がよく聞こえません。
sentence_meaning: Her hearing isn't very good.

mnemonic: 生 the shoot pushing its way up, except this time nobody is doing it to anybody. The phone goes at four in the morning and there is a new person in the world: うまれる.
notes: 生む うむ is bearing the child; 生まれる is the child arriving. 生まれ うまれ on its own is where you are from.
sentence: 友達に子供が生まれました。
sentence_meaning: My friend had a baby.

mnemonic: 禾 grain being shifted about in 多 quantity, and 動 heavy things moved by force. Not a stroll. Getting an entire party and its luggage from one place to the next: いどう.
notes: 移動する is moving from place to place. 引っ越す ひっこす is moving house.
sentence: 私たちはレンタカーで移動しました。
sentence_meaning: We traveled around by a rental car.

mnemonic: 牙 a fang, 阝 a mound, and 魔 the demon out of 魔法 alongside. The suitcase is in the hall and everybody has to go round it. A jam, and somebody's fault: じゃま.
notes: 邪魔する is to get in the way. お邪魔します is said entering somebody's home, apologising for being the obstacle.
sentence: この大きい荷物はとても邪魔です。
sentence_meaning: This big luggage is a big hindrance.

mnemonic: 辶 a road with no destination attached to it. Nobody has told them what the game is and nobody needs to. Two hours in the park and not one plan between them: あそぶ.
notes: Covers playing and going out to enjoy yourself. 遊びに行く is going round to somebody's, not necessarily to play.
sentence: 子供たちが公園で遊んでいる。
sentence_meaning: The children are playing in the park.

mnemonic: 要 the part everything else hangs off, out of 必要. Walk in off the street with no booking and they seat you anyway. Whatever it was, it was not needed: いる.
notes: Same reading as いる, to exist, and usually written in kana, so context does the work. It takes が: お金が要る.
sentence: 予約は要りません。
sentence_meaning: Reservations are not required.

meaning: to be lost, to be used up
mnemonic: 無 the whole lot burnt away to nothing, with なる the turning into. It was there this morning. Where it went has stopped being the interesting question: なくなる.
notes: Used up or gone missing, both. Careful with 亡くなる なくなる, identical in speech, which is the polite word for somebody dying.
sentence: もうお金が無くなりました。
sentence_meaning: I've run out of money already.

mnemonic: 口 a mouth down at the bottom, which is why the word opens with くち. The visible edge of it, and hers are the part everybody comments on: くちびる.
notes: 口 くち is the mouth and 唇 くちびる begins with it. リップ is the loanword on the cosmetics.
sentence: 彼女の唇はとても可愛いです。
sentence_meaning: Her lips are really cute.

mnemonic: 着 the same character as arriving, because this is clothes arriving on you. Suit on at seven for a nine o'clock meeting, and it stays on until midnight: きる.
notes: Worn on the upper or whole body. 履く はく is anything below the waist. Same reading as 切る きる, to cut, which the kanji keeps apart.
sentence: 今日はスーツを着ています。
sentence_meaning: I'm wearing a suit today.

mnemonic: 色 a colour, and 々 saying do that one again, so colours upon colours. He knows a bit about everything and intends to cover all of it: いろいろ.
notes: 々 means repeat the character before it, so this is 色色. It comes back six more times in this deck, in 人々, 我々, 日々, 少々, 元々 and 様々.
sentence: 彼は色々なことを知っている。
sentence_meaning: He knows about a lot of things.

mnemonic: He holds the door open with his back and waits. Nothing is said and nothing needs saying, because the whole invitation is in the eyebrows: どうぞ.
notes: Offers and invites: take it, go ahead, after you. どうも is thanks, and the two get muddled constantly.
sentence: こちらへどうぞ。
sentence_meaning: This way please.

mnemonic: 立つ standing and 上がる going up, welded together. He was sat down a second ago, the chair has scraped, and the whole table has stopped talking: たちあがる.
notes: Both halves are words you already have. It is also what a computer does when it boots.
sentence: 彼は急に立ち上がったの。
sentence_meaning: He suddenly stood up.

mnemonic: 田 a field sat on 心 a heart, and this is what stays up there rather than what you do about it. He asked her, and asking cost him everything he had: おもい.
notes: The thought or feeling itself, from 思う おもう. Later comes 重い おもい, heavy, which sounds identical.
sentence: 必死の思いで彼に頼んだよ。
sentence_meaning: I asked him out of desperation.

mnemonic: 以 the marker that fixes a boundary, and 前 everything in front of it. He lived here once, on the far side of that line, and the shop still remembers him: いぜん.
notes: Same 以 as 以上 and 以外. 以前 is before some point; 前 まえ on its own is simply ago.
sentence: 以前彼はこの町に住んでいたんだ。
sentence_meaning: He used to live in this town.

meaning: a little more, a bit more
mnemonic: もう pointed forwards, and 少し the scooch left in the glass. Not slower. A bit slower, and he is asking nicely because he stopped following two sentences ago: もうすこし.
notes: Both halves are already in the deck. もうちょっと is the casual version of the same request.
sentence: もう少しゆっくり話してください。
sentence_meaning: Please speak a little slower.

mnemonic: A dragon with 衣 clothing under it, arriving from above and giving nobody a say. The climbers heard nothing until it was already between them and the tents: おそう.
notes: Used of animals, weather and crime. 攻撃 こうげき is a deliberate assault, and more military.
sentence: 山で登山客が熊に襲われたよ。
sentence_meaning: Some climbers were attacked by a bear in the mountains.

meaning: to be found, to be caught
mnemonic: 見 an eye and 付 a hand fixing onto what it saw, the same as 見つける, except nobody is looking. The glasses turn up or they do not, and today they do not: みつかる.
notes: 見つける みつける is you finding it. 見つかる is it being found, or you being caught.
sentence: メガネが見つかりません。
sentence_meaning: I can't find my glasses.

mnemonic: A hand snatching down at a heart, the same 急 you have as きゅう. Fifteen minutes to cross town, and he is putting his coat on inside the lift: いそぐ.
notes: Same 急 as 急 きゅう, sudden. 急いで いそいで is quickly, said as an instruction.
sentence: 時間がないので、急いでください。
sentence_meaning: We don't have much time, so please hurry.

mnemonic: Two trains and a bus to get here, and now you are talking about leaving. Sit down. The effort is spent either way, so spend the afternoon too: せっかく.
notes: Marks effort already made that would otherwise go to waste. せっかくだから is since we are here anyway.
sentence: せっかく来たんだからゆっくりして行きなさい。
sentence_meaning: Since you've come all the way, why don't you stay for a while?

meaning: to get off, to go down
mnemonic: 阝 a mound, and somebody picking their way down off it. The bus is still moving and you are already at the door with a hand on the rail: おりる.
notes: Same reading as 下りる おりる. 降りる is getting off or out of something: a bus, a train, a car.
sentence: ここでバスを降ります。
sentence_meaning: I'm getting off the bus here.

meaning: to go down, to come down
mnemonic: The same おりる, written with 下, the mark that sits below the line. Not off anything. Simply down, one stair at a time, at the end of the corridor: おりる.
notes: Same reading as 降りる おりる. 下りる is going down stairs or a hill; 降りる is getting off a vehicle.
sentence: そこの階段を下りてください。
sentence_meaning: Please go down those stairs.

mnemonic: 刀 a blade on the right, and everything to its left is what the blade meets. Fold the paper, run a thumb down the crease, then take the scissors to it: きる.
notes: Same reading as 着る きる, to wear. Also switching off and cutting off: 電話を切る is hanging up.
sentence: この紙を半分に切ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please cut this paper in half.
